newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Issue Department has 2.8 bln mark assets.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Issue Department has 2.8 bln mark assets.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank's Issue Department, the core of a currency board system designed to help revive the economy, entered the arrangement on Tuesday with 2.8 billion mark in assets and liabilities, the BNB said.

The department's assets worth 2.819 trillion levs include mark equivalent 1.46 trillion levs in securities, 701 billion levs cash and nostro accounts in foreign currencies, 640.7 billion levs in monetary gold and 11.8 billion levs in accrued intrest receivable, said the BNB in a statement.

The department's liabilities, estimated at 2.819 trillion levs, comprise 598.9 billion lev currency in circulation, 529.4 billion levs in bank deposits and current accounts, 597.9 billion levs in government deposits and accounts, 555.8 billion levs in a State Fund for Reconstruction and Development account, 33 billion levs in other deposits and accrued interest payable of 10.2 billion levs.

These liabilities also include a 493.8 billion lev deposit of the BNB Banking Department that can be used for lending to sound banks, only when the functioning of the banking and payments system is threatened.
The primary objective of the Banking Department is to ensure confidence in the liquidity of the the banking system and more broadly the efficient funcitoning of key financial markets.

Under an agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Bulgaria introduced on Tuesday a fixed exchange rate mechanism which requires levs in circulation be matched by the BNB foreign exchange reserves, known as currency board.
Under the arrangement the lev is pegged to the mark as anchor at 1,000 levs. The system bans central bank lending to the government and commercial banks.
The balance sheet will be published weekly. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
